note: Adjudicated accidental variants: one of punctuation and one of orthography (the house i/j rule). Substantive text agrees across both witnesses with zero divergence.

adjudicated.ruling: No comma before the relative, with handmissal-eo and with the corpus ruling at ordinarium.sanctus w017: qui lætíficat defines the God addressed rather than adding a remark about him, and the antiphon is said as one unbroken phrase. DO's comma follows the Clementine punctuation of Ps 42:4.

The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the 1962 typical edition sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Mszał Rzymski of the Tyniec Benedictines (Pallottinum, Poznań 1963), which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.
